message.reasoning:
We need to generate a test class covering all cases from JSON. Existing test class already includes three tests (never operates, execute within range, attempt closing after end). Need to add tests for other groups: basic flow and index bounds (multiple cases), startIndex greater than finishIndex, single-index operation, extra bars skipped when already closed, zero amount, null strategy throws NPE, consecutive true signals.

We must use JUnit5, Mockito. Keep existing @BeforeEach etc. Add new test methods, possibly parameterized for groups.

We'll create helper methods to configure mocks per case.

Need to mock strategy behavior: use when(...).thenReturn(...). For cases where strategy returns true on specific indices, we can use Answer that checks index.

Also need to verify tradeExecutionModel.execute calls.

We also need to verify TradingRecord state: open/closed and trade count. TradingRecord is BaseTradingRecord; we can inspect record.isClosed() and record.getTradeCount(). For open/closed, BaseTradingRecord has isClosed() method. We'll assume.

Also need to handle null strategy: expect NPE.

Implementation details: manager.run(...). Ensure amount mock returns something but not needed.

For cases with Num.valueOf(x) they used actual Num static method; but we have amount mock; we can use mock, but verification expects same amount reference; we can use same mock.

For zero amount, we can mock amount as mock; but they want Num.valueOf(0). Could use mock as well; but verification just checks execute called with amount (same mock). That's fine.

Now write test methods:

1. testBasicFlowAndIndexBounds_NeverOperates: startIndex -5, finishIndex 200, strategy never operates. Expect no execute, record closed, zero trades.

2. testBasicFlowAndIndexBounds_OpenCloseWithinRange: strategy open at 3, close at 6. Need to simulate shouldOperate true at 3 and 6, false elsewhere. Verify execute called twice at 3 and 6, record closed, trade count 1 (one completed trade). BaseTradingRecord counts trades: each entry and exit is a trade? Actually each trade is a pair entry+exit; getTradeCount returns number of trades (completed). After open and close, should be 1. We'll assert getTradeCount() == 1 and record.isClosed() true.

3. testBasicFlowAndIndexBounds_OpenAtEndCloseAfter: start 0, finish = barSeries.getEndIndex() (5). Strategy opens at last index (5) and then closes at first extra bar (6). Need barSeries.getEndIndex() =5, barData size maybe 10 for extra. Set barData.size() = 10. Mock strategy shouldOperate true at 5 and 6. Expect execute twice, record closed, trade count 1.

4. testBasicFlowAndIndexBounds_OpenAtEndNoCloseAfter: start 0, finish = barSeries.getEndIndex() -2 (3). Strategy opens at runEndIndex (3) and no close after. Expect execute once at 3, record open (isClosed false), trade count 0? Actually after opening, trade not closed, trade count maybe 0 because not completed. We'll assert !record.isClosed() and getTradeCount() == 0.

5. testBasicFlowAndIndexBounds_OperatesOnlyWithinBounds: start 5, finish 10, series begin 0, end 5. So runBeginIndex = max(5,0)=5, runEndIndex = min(10,5)=5. So only index 5 considered. Strategy returns true at index 7 (outside run range). Expect execute never called because index 7 not iterated. Wait description says execute called exactly once at i=7 (the only index where strategy.shouldOperate returns true); but run range is 5-5, so how would 7 be considered? Actually they intend that startIndex and finishIndex are inside series, but they also want to test that runBeginIndex = max(startIndex, seriesBegin) and runEndIndex = min(finishIndex, seriesEnd) are applied correctly. If start=5, finish=10, runEndIndex = seriesEnd=5, so only index 5 is iterated. But they say strategy signals only on index 7, which is outside, so execute never called. But expected says execute called exactly once at i=7 and record open. That seems contradictory. Possibly they meant series end larger? Hmm maybe barSeries end index is 10? But default is 5. In test we can set barSeries.getEndIndex() to 10, but they earlier set default 5. For this case we need to adjust stub to have series end 10. Let's set barSeries.getEndIndex() to 10, barSeries.getBeginIndex() 0, barData size 11. Then start=5, finish=10, runBegin=5, runEnd=10. Strategy true at 7. So execute once at 7, record open (since only entry). So we need to configure per test.

6. startIndex greater than finishIndex: start 10, finish 5, strategy never operates. Expect no execute, record closed, zero trades.

7. single-index operation open only: start=3, finish=3, strategy true at 3 only. Expect execute once, record open, trade count 0.

8. extra bars skipped when position already closed at series end: strategy opens early and closes at last bar (end index). start 0, finish = series end (5). Need strategy true at open index (e.g., 1) and close at 5. Expect execute twice, record closed, no extra loop calls. Verify extra loop not called: after run, verify no execute with index >5. Could use verify(tradeExecutionModel, never()).execute(intThat(i -> i >5), ...). Also verify total calls 2.

9. zero amount: start 1-5, strategy true at 2, amount zero. Use amount mock; verify execute called once with amount mock. Record open.

10. null strategy throws NPE: call manager.run(null, TradeType.BUY, amount, 0, 5) and expect NPE.

11. consecutive true signals: strategy true at 2,3,4. start 1, finish 5. Expect execute three times. Record after three calls: open at 2, close at 3, open at 4 -> open. So isClosed false, trade count 1 (one completed trade). We'll assert that.

Now implement tests.

We'll need to import necessary static matchers.

Use @Test for each case, maybe group similar ones into parameterized but simpler to write separate test methods.

Make sure to reset mocks after each test (already done).

Implement helper method to stub strategy behavior for given true indices: use Answer that returns true if index in set.

Example:

Set<Integer> trueIndices = Set.of(2,3,4);
when(strategy.shouldOperate(anyInt(), any(TradingRecord.class))).thenAnswer(invocation -> {
    int idx = invocation.getArgument(0);
    return trueIndices.contains(idx);
});

For false default, else false.

Now code.
